==Ingredients==

=== Pudding ===
* 200 g [[Cookbook:Sweetened Condensed Milk|sweetened condensed milk]]
* 200 g natural set or Greek [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of green [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] powder
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Pistachio|pistachio]] nuts, cut into slivers
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]], soaked in warm water for 10 minutes, then drained

=== '''Figs in syrup''' ===
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* 300 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] water
* Finely-pared zest of 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
* 1 teaspoon lemon juice
* 2 [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* 2.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] piece cassia bark or [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] stick
* 1 [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]] pod
* 4 ripe [[Cookbook:Fig|figs]]
==Procedure==
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 150°C (130°C fan oven), mark 2. Line four [[Cookbook:Ramekin|ramekins]] with paper [[Cookbook:Cupcake Liner|muffin cases]].
# [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] the condensed milk, yoghurt, and cardamom powder together in a bowl, then fold in the pistachios and raisins. Pour the mixture into the lined ramekins. Stand them in a roasting tin and pour enough warm water into the tin to come almost halfway up the sides of the moulds. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the oven for 40–45 minutes until set.
# Meanwhile, prepare the figs. Put the sugar, water, lemon zest and juice, and spices into a heavy-based pan. Cook over low heat until the sugar has dissolved, then gradually bring to the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# In the meantime, cut each fig vertically into four. Add the figs to the sugar syrup and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for two minutes, then take the pan off the heat. Leave the figs to cool in syrup.
# On removing the baked puddings from the oven, take the ramekins out of the water-bath and set aside to cool.
# To serve, unmould the puddings on to serving plates, arrange the figs on top, and drizzle the poaching syrup around the plates.
